accepted.sentence: Heavier reference volumes are usually placed on lower tiers, keeping the center of mass low and improving stability.
Leaving a little headroom above upright volumes makes them easier to grasp and remove without scraping the level above.
When adding new acquisitions, staff may shift neighboring items aside before inserting each volume in its intended sequence.
Small labels along front edges can identify subject sections, helping users return items to the correct location.
Libraries may display selected titles with their covers facing outward to draw attention to particular recommendations or new arrivals.
During inventory, workers scan spines in sequence and compare entries with a catalog to find misplaced volumes.
Leaving an unoccupied section beside a growing collection allows new arrivals to be added without reorganizing the entire arrangement.
After assembly, a gentle push at an upper corner can reveal wobbling that needs correction before the unit is loaded.
